parts.name: Parametric stepped shaft with optional keyway
Keyed shaft (DIN 6885)
Threaded shaft (lead screw)
Splined shaft (DIN 5480 external involute spline)

fit_guidance_mm.tip_clearance: 0.1 to 0.2 mm on diameter for sliding or fixed fits
fit_guidance_mm.side_fit: H7/js6 or H7/k6 for close fits per DIN 5480

required_features: polygon() 2D profile using list comprehension with for/let/each
Alternating root and outer radius points per tooth
Optional end chamfer using difference() with tapered cylinders
design_rules: Use polygon() with for/let/each list comprehension — do NOT use difference() to cut tooth spaces from a solid disc.
Each tooth contributes 4 polygon points: valley-entry, tip-start, tip-end, valley-exit.
root_d is the valley (minor) diameter; outer_d is the tooth tip (major) diameter.
tooth_fill controls tooth arc width: 0.50 = equal tooth and gap.
Rotate 90 degrees before linear_extrude so the shaft axis lies along X (or keep along Z without the rotate).
Set  = 160 or higher for smooth circular interpolation.
validation_criteria: splined_shaft module present
difference() applied to a 2D circle(r=r_tip) with tooth-space polygons
z evenly spaced tooth spaces present
polygon corners use r_root and r_tip with pressure-angle-derived angles
linear_extrude present for shaft length
failure_modes: cube teeth added to a root cylinder — produces rectangular protrusions, not spline teeth
translate([r,0,0]) cube(...) pattern — off-axis boxes are not spline teeth
no tooth-space difference, only a plain cylinder

parts.name: Transmission shaft with gears.scad helical gears
required_features: Multiple coaxial helical gears generated with gears.scad spur_gear()
Alternating helix directions on gear sections
Thread ring details at the output end
Radial cross hole through the end journal
design_rules: For transmission shaft, countershaft, gearbox shaft, or gear shaft requests, use this exact gears.scad-based pattern unless the user explicitly asks for a different construction.
Use the project gear library: use <D:/downloads/openscad_copilot (1)/openscad_copilot/gears.scad> and call spur_gear(..., helix_angle=...) through library_helical_gear().
Never hand-build transmission-shaft gear teeth from cubes, rectangular blocks, or simple radial boxes.
Do not define a custom block-tooth module gear(...) for this family.
Keep all shaft steps, library gears, splines, shoulders, thread rings, and the radial cross-hole on one coaxial shaft axis.
Do not reference undeclared gear variables such as gear_teeth3.
Do not assign geometry to variables. OpenSCAD geometry statements cannot be stored in variables.
Do not declare string metadata variables such as manufacturing = "fdm" in OpenSCAD code.
Use explicit fixed positions from the RAG example for shaft sections and gears; do not compute shaft_pos by appending to an array.
OpenSCAD variables are immutable. NEVER write shaft_pos = [0]; for (...) shaft_pos = concat(...). Use fixed numeric positions or a pure recursive function instead.

Do not wrap spur_gear() in a gear_assembly() module that subtracts shaft bores and adds hubs unless the user explicitly asks for loose gears; the RAG pattern uses bore=0 so gears fuse to the shaft assembly.
failure_modes: gear teeth hand-built from rectangular cubes instead of gears.scad spur_gear()
custom module gear(...) with block teeth used for transmission shaft gears
undefined gear_teeth3 or other missing gear parameter referenced
plain hollow tube or smooth cylinder returned for a transmission shaft request
transmission shaft housing returned instead of the rotating gear shaft
loose gears placed beside the shaft instead of coaxially mounted on it
missing spline sections or output thread/end details
geometry assigned to variables instead of emitted directly in modules
shaft_pos = [0]; for (...) shaft_pos = concat(...) used; OpenSCAD cannot reassign variables this way
gear_assembly() adds hubs and subtracts shaft bores instead of using the RAG library_helical_gear() pattern with bore=0
array-driven generated positions drift from the fixed-position shaft_transmission RAG example
validation_criteria: gears.scad is included with use or include
library_helical_gear module present
spur_gear() is called for each transmission gear section
helix_angle parameter is used on gear calls
no custom rectangular-tooth module gear() is present
no cube teeth in the gear module
gear_teeth3 is not referenced
spline sections present
thread rings present
cross hole subtraction present
fixed numeric shaft_section positions are used
no shaft_pos = concat(...) reassignment pattern
no gear_assembly() bore-subtracting wrapper replaces library_helical_gear()

parts.name: Parametric line shaft with pulleys
required_features: Two keyed shaft sections with subtractive keyways
Two coaxial pulleys mounted on the shaft
Simplified threaded end represented by narrow rings
design_rules: A line shaft should be a long rotating shaft carrying pulleys or belt-drive elements, not just a short plain cylinder with one keyway.
Use the full line-shaft assembly pattern: main shaft, bearing seats, keyed sections, coaxial pulleys, and simplified threaded end rings.
Keep all shaft sections, bearing seats, pulleys, and thread rings coaxial on the same shaft axis.
Use subtractive keyways on keyed sections with a direct difference() block; do not store the shaft or slot geometry in variables.
Pulleys are positive coaxial geometry with a bore through their center.
Threaded ends can be represented by repeated narrow rings when detailed thread geometry is not required.
OpenSCAD geometry cannot be assigned to variables. NEVER write shaft = cylinder(...), slot = translate(...) cube(...), body = union(){...}, or result = difference(){...}.
If helper modules are needed, define module shaft_section(...), module keyed_section(...), and module pulley(...), then call those modules directly inside union() or difference().
Do not declare string metadata variables such as manufacturing = "fdm" in OpenSCAD code.
failure_modes: plain smooth cylinder returned for a line shaft request
short keyed shaft returned instead of the full line shaft assembly
shaft = cylinder(...) or slot = translate(...) cube(...) used; OpenSCAD geometry assignment is invalid
pulleys omitted from the line shaft
pulleys placed beside the shaft instead of coaxially mounted
keyed sections missing their subtractive keyway cuts
bearing seats missing or not coaxial with the main shaft
line shaft confused with transmission countershaft with gears
geometry assigned to variables instead of emitted directly in modules
validation_criteria: module line_shaft() present
shaft_section module present
keyed_section module uses difference() directly
pulley module present and called at least twice
bearing_seat called near both shaft ends
threaded end represented by repeated narrow shaft_section rings
no geometry assignment such as shaft = cylinder or slot = translate
